conflicts.fact: Trend in first ionisation energy across Period 3 and its use to explain reactivity (Al value)
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 says IE has a dip at Al (Al lower than Mg), and Lesson 6 quotes Mg 738 and Al 577 (Al lower than Mg), yet Lesson 6 says Al and Si have higher ionisation energies than Mg/Na and explains that unreactivity as a steadily increasing effective nuclear charge and higher IE. Lesson 7 says IE increases with decreasing reactivity across Na→Mg→Al, ignoring that Al's IE is lower than Mg's.

conflicts.fact: Number of inner shielding electrons for sodium vs the ground-state configuration
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 says sodium has 2 full inner shells; Lesson 7 says sodium's outer electron is shielded by 10 inner electrons (consistent), but Lesson 7 says magnesium is shielded by only 10 inner electrons yet also asserts potassium is shielded by 18 - consistent; no real conflict beyond claims about shielding being 'same' across period while Lesson 3 attributes Group II difference to nuclear charge. (low significance)

conflicts.fact: Where Period 3 ionisation energy was measured/learned and the configuration of aluminium
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 teacher asks 'What electron configuration did we write for aluminium in Lesson 3?' but Lesson 3 only drew Na, Mg, Ca, K diagrams (no Al); Lesson 7 DQB answer says 'we measured ionisation energies across Period 3 in Lesson 3', whereas Period 3 IE was plotted in Lesson 5.

Lesson 1 has students start a model in Lesson 1 and Lesson 3 says it was started in Lesson 1; Lesson 6 says the cumulative annotated periodic table model was started in Lesson 2; Lesson 5 says it began in Lesson 1 as a Na atom diagram.

conflicts.fact: Which lesson dealt with sodium/water observations vs Group I trend (lithium reaction as sodium comparison) and Lesson 4's chlorine reactivity claim
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 claims chlorine is chosen at Kisumu because it has the highest electron affinity among the three, and Lesson 4 says chlorine is the most reactive 'aqueous halogen'; Lesson 4 also ties argon to 'going right across the period' as an extension of the halogen trend, while Lesson 5 explains argon's inertness via full shell and ionisation energy. Lesson 4 says the full-shell reactivity via electron gain is 'impossible', whereas Lesson 7 says argon has 'no tendency to gain or lose' — compatible.

Lesson 2 says hydrogen relights a glowing splint; Lessons 3 and 6 say it gives a squeaky pop with a lighted splint (Lesson 6 also asks students to test with a glowing splint while observed result is a pop).

conflicts.fact: Calcium hydroxide / magnesium cold-water reaction product states and pH
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 and 6 describe magnesium barely fizzing in cold water; Lesson 3 gives Mg(OH)2 formed and faintly alkaline (pH 9–10) while Lesson 3 equation lists Ca(OH)2(aq) vs Mg(OH)2(s), a minor inconsistency in treatment of hydroxide solubility.
